texts.content_exam:
Iguazu Falls are located on the Iguazu River and an area shared by Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay, so it is a three-country border zone. You can travel to the city Foz do Iguacu on the Brazilian side, or the town Puerto Iguazu, on the Argentine side. Both cities have airports, bus stations and rental car agencies, so you can choose to go by plane, bus or car.

Iguazu National Park offers many activities to make your adventure unforgettable. You can experience the waterfalls in different ways; go on a trekking tour, take a helicopter ride above the Iguazu Falls, go canoeing in the Iguazu river.

texts.content_exam:
The World Tour Agency said that many people had visited the Iguazu Falls. They told us that the Falls had been so beautiful and could be ranked as one of the ten best places in the world. Tourists said that the Falls they had seen were unique landmarks.

They also said that some tourists had found the Falls wonderful with their sub-tropical climate and rains all year. Others said that fresh fruit had been one of the key delights for travellers besides a variety of dishes such as black beans stew, seafood stew and mixed grilled meats. They added that the food at the open market had been good and cheap that tourists decided to have all their meals there.

Travel experts consider that Iguazu is a magnificent holiday destination for adventure and nature lovers.

texts.content_exam:
Helen Adame Keller was born a healthy child in Alabama, on June 27, 1880. At the age of 19 months, Helen became deaf and blind as a result of scarlet fever. As Helen grew from the time being a baby into childhood, she became wild. She would kick and scream when angry, and giggle when happy.

Her family wanted their daughter to learn. They decided to help her and met the school's director who suggested a teacher who was called Ann Sullivan to work with Helen. Sullivan went to Keller's home in Alabama. Helen was six years old when Sullivan began to teach her finger spelling. She started by bringing Helen a doll to touch and spell the word "doll".

texts.content_exam:
At first, Keller refused to cooperate with Sullivan's instruction. Finally, Sullivan asked Helen's parents to allow her with Helen alone, so that Keller could concentrate only on Sullivan's instruction. Therefore, Sullivan and Helen moved to a nearby cottage.

After a great struggle with Helen, a surprising event happened. Sullivan taught Keller the word "water"; she helped her make the connection between the object and the letters by taking Helen out to the water pump, and placing Keller's hand under the water. While Sullivan was flushing cool water over Keller's hand, she spelled out the word w-a-t-e-r. By nightfall, she had learned 30 words.

Helen Keller overcame the difficult situation of being blind and deaf to become a famous American educator in the 20th century.
